jurisdictions.name: Portland
notes: The city's pool page says a building permit is needed before installing a swimming pool, defined as a structure holding water over 24 inches deep, unless the pool is prefabricated with walls entirely above adjacent grade.
An electrical permit is required for in-ground pools, and the permit application forms listed are the building, electrical and mechanical permit applications.
The page calls for a barrier at least 4 ft high, a maximum 2 inch gap under it, openings that do not pass a 4 inch sphere, and a self-closing, latching gate that opens outward.
The pool must be at least 3 feet from any lot line, set back from adjacent slopes, and may face extra zoning limits in an overlay zone or plan district.

sources.title: Hot Tubs, Ponds, Swimming Pools, and Water Features (Portland.gov)

jurisdictions.name: Medford
jurisdictions.office: City of Medford Building Safety Department
notes: The pool submittal guidelines ask for a building permit application, a Pool Barrier Acknowledgement form, and a to-scale site plan showing utility easements, setbacks and mechanical equipment location.
Site and pool construction documents must be at least 11x17, while engineering calculations and geotechnical reports may be 8.5x11.
The plans must state pool type (in-ground or above ground), depth, sand or cartridge filter, whether heated, and the auto fill and backflow device.
The final inspection checks a barrier at least 48 inches high, openings that stop a 4 inch sphere, and outward-opening self-latching, self-closing gates.
Medford requires a 4-foot high temporary or permanent fence around swimming pool excavations.

sources.title: Swimming Pool Submittal Guidelines and Swimming Pool Safety (City of Medford)

jurisdictions.name: Gresham
notes: Gresham's list of work not needing a permit exempts prefabricated pools in R-3 occupancies where the pool walls are entirely above the adjacent grade.
The same list says the barrier requirements in Appendix G are not exempt, so barriers around swimming pools still need a permit.
The list excludes pool barriers from its exemption for fences not over 7 feet high.

sources.title: Projects That Do Not Require Permits (City of Gresham)

state_level.note: Oregon Building Codes Division says a fence serving as a barrier around a swimming pool, hot tub or spa needs a residential building permit, and barriers around prefabricated above-grade pools are not exempt.

source.title: About Oregon residential building permits (Building Codes Division)
